prompt: An unretouched outdoor photograph of one real adult person, not a painting, not concept art. A long, straight, muddy mountain-forest path climbs directly away from the camera up a steady slope through tall straight fir trees. The near ground fills the lower third of the frame and is in sharp focus: soft, wet, dark brown mud with a fresh line of boot prints walking away from us up the middle of the path. Water stands in some of the prints. Beside every second print is a small, round, deep hole punched in the mud by the foot of a walking staff. The prints lead up the path to one person, about two thirds of the way up the frame, who walks away from us seen from directly behind. They are small in the frame but completely whole, from the tip of the hood to the boots, with a strip of muddy path visible below their feet. They are mid-stride, with the left foot forward and loading, and the right arm reaching ahead to plant a plain dark blackthorn staff, taller than their shoulder, whose foot is just meeting the mud ahead of them. The garment is a long hooded robe of undyed natural brown-black sheep's wool, a dark rusty peat-brown, matte and heavy, falling in long vertical folds to the ankles. The hood is up and the face is entirely hidden, turned away uphill. The hem is wet and darker still, splashed with mud, and dark leather boots show beneath it. Ground: wet mud, puddles in the ruts, flattened brown needles and leaves at the path edges, wet moss and a few exposed roots, all readable and sharp around the near prints and around the walker's feet. Large dark fir trunks stand close on both sides in the foreground. Light: soft overcast daylight from the upper left. The top of the hood and the left shoulder catch the most light, folds shade to the lower right, and every shadow is soft. Behind the walker: the path disappears into mist, and the trunks beyond them fade in at least three distinct layers from dark grey to pale grey to nearly white. The mist starts beyond the figure and never reaches their feet or the near ground. Camera: a 50mm lens at standing eye level from far down the path, with deep focus from the near prints to the walker. Colour: muted and natural, dark brown wool, brown mud, grey-green fir and pale mist, with no saturated colour anywhere. A plain, slightly flat walker's snapshot with natural grain. Their right arm reaches forward and up, and the hand grips a plain hazel walking staff a little taller than their shoulder, with grey-brown bark and a rubbed, paler grip. Nothing of the face shows: the hood is turned uphill and away, and only the soft curve of the back of a head shows through the wool. The bottom of the robe, from the hem to mid-calf, is soaked darker, a wet grey-brown, where it has dragged through wet bracken, and it clings a little to the calves. It is flecked with black mud and bits of brown beech leaf. Under the hem show worn brown leather lace-up boots, dark with wet, with rolled grey wool socks at the top. Behind and above: the path climbs on into mist between smooth pale beech trunks, which fade in at least three layers, from silver-grey to almost white, and the mist stays behind the figure, clear of the feet and the near ground. Camera: a 35mm lens at a low eye level from just below, the whole figure in frame from the tip of the hood to below both boots.
